assignments.title: Plan Tuesday Release — FindCare Product: Provider Search, Safety Filter, Maps, Angular Port
assignments.description:
You are the Enterprise Architect for ChatHealthy operating under framework_02.

This assignment corrects ASN-5EE93C. That assignment gave you only Brain infrastructure context. This assignment gives you the full product picture. Plan Tuesday's release against what the Boss actually wants to ship.

---

WHAT CHATHEALTHY IS:
ChatHealthy is a consumer healthcare navigation product. The core product is FindCare — a chat interface that helps consumers find healthcare providers (doctors, specialists, clinics) near them. The user describes what they need in natural language, the system finds matching providers, and shows them on a map.

---

WHAT EXISTS TODAY (live on HuggingFace, Gradio-based, ~1050 lines in app.py):

1. SAFETY FILTER — dual detection: keyword list (chest pain, stroke, etc.) + Haiku semantic check. KNOWN BUG: Haiku was triggering on vague pain statements like 'I'm in pain' and blocking the conversation. This was tightened in a recent commit but needs validation. Safety incidents are logged to MongoDB Safety.emergency_incidents. This feature is critical — it must ship.

2. PROVIDER SEARCH — find_providers(specialty_query, state, city) queries providers_staging collection in MongoDB. find_specialty_codes(query) maps user language to NPI taxonomy codes using vector search + regex fallback. KNOWN BUG: MongoDB connection fails on HuggingFace because MONGO_connectionString is not available as a HuggingFace secret. Provider search silently returns empty. This is the primary blocker.

3. NO GOOGLE MAPS — provider results are returned as text only. No map rendering exists. This is new work.

4. CLINICAL TRIALS SEARCH — search_clinical_trials() calls ClinicalTrials.gov API. Works but is a secondary feature.

5. ABOUT US / CONTACT — records user contact details to MongoDB AboutUs.lead. Works.

Supported states: Delaware (DE) and Mississippi (MS) only.

---

WHAT THE BOSS WANTS FOR TUESDAY MARCH 30:

1. Provider search working end-to-end: user asks for a provider in natural language → system finds matching providers from MongoDB → results shown in chat
2. Safety filter validated: health questions pass through; only genuine emergencies are escalated
3. Google Maps: provider results include a map showing provider locations
4. Angular frontend: port from Gradio to Angular + FastAPI. This replaces the partial React shell that exists at Code/ConversationalUX/FindCareChat/frontend/. The new stack is Angular (frontend) + FastAPI (Python backend). FastAPI replaces Gradio.

Brain Loop 0.1 is operational infrastructure — it is NOT a user-facing Tuesday deliverable. Do not plan Brain Loop as a Tuesday feature.

---

ARCHITECTURE CONSTRAINTS (from Machine Brain and framework_02):
- Three-application rule: Website (Cloudflare, static), Chat (HuggingFace/Azure, Angular+FastAPI), DataPipelines (Azure Functions). These boundaries are hard.
- App 2 (Chat) reads from MongoDB freely. Never writes to PublicHealthData.
- App 3 (DataPipelines) owns all PublicHealthData writes.
- Frontend hosting: Cloudflare Pages (NOT Azure Static Web Apps — CFO directive).
- FastAPI backend: Azure App Service B1.
- ENV_PREFIX (dev/qa/prod) controls all database routing — not yet implemented in the Chat app.

---

YOUR DELIVERABLES:
1. Feature set — what ships Tuesday 2026-03-30, what does not, with specific reasons
2. Test schedule — phases and timing with dates
3. Acceptance criteria — minimum 3 per feature, covering distinct behavioral dimensions
4. End-to-end user flows — minimum 3, covering the full user journey from question to map
5. UAT scenarios — per acceptance criterion, per UAT rules below
6. Risk and gate recommendation — your honest assessment

Include your usage block. Return raw JSON only matching the Assurance Output schema.

assignments.description:
Port the production Gradio app at Code/ConversationalUX/ChatHealthyWhoAmIChat/app.py
to the FastAPI + React stack at Code/ConversationalUX/FindCareChat/.

FIRST: Read app.py in full. List any functionality you find that is NOT covered
by boss_scope in your review pack tradeoff_suggestions — Boss must decide.

WHAT IS ALREADY BUILT (do NOT rewrite):
- backend/main.py: safety filter, provider search tools, clinical trials, HIPAA
  consent flow, de-identification, MongoDB, SparkPost notifications — all ported.
- frontend/src/: ChatWindow + MessageBubble React shell with emergency lock,
  markdown rendering, loading state.

WHAT YOU MUST COMPLETE:

1. SWITCH CHAT ENGINE — Replace gpt-4o-mini with Claude claude-sonnet-4-6:
   - Replace OpenAI client.chat.completions.create() with Anthropic messages.create()
   - Re-define all 6 tool schemas in Anthropic format (input_schema, not parameters)
   - Replace OpenAI tool_calls loop with Anthropic tool_use content block loop
   - Haiku stays for: safety check, query expansion, summarization, de-identification

2. COMPLETE POST /chat ENDPOINT:
   - Input: {message: str, history: [{role, content}]}
   - Output: {response: str, emergency: bool}
   - Read client IP from FastAPI Request object for emergency lock checks
   - Check IP lock (in-memory + MongoDB) and session lock (scan history) before chat
   - Admin unlock: detect "UNLOCK:<ADMIN_UNLOCK_KEY>" and clear lock
   - Follow-up check: every 5th user message, insert system message prompting
     the follow-up offer (same logic as Gradio lines 1002-1010)

3. SYSTEM PROMPT + CONTEXT:
   - Implement _load_me_context(): load me/summary.txt, me/*.pdf (via pypdf),
     me/findcare-code-package.json — same as Gradio Me.build_context()
   - Build system prompt with all 7 rules (EMERGENCY, SOURCE RESTRICTION, NO HEDGING,
     MEDICAL vs NAVIGATION, TOOL CALL ORDER, MULTIPLE QUESTIONS, CODEBASE CONTEXT)
   - Skip Snow character, source restriction, ChatHealthy context

4. ENV_PREFIX ROUTING:
   - Every MongoDB db["DatabaseName"] reference must use ENV_PREFIX:
     db[f"{ENV_PREFIX}_DatabaseName"]
   - ENV_PREFIX = os.getenv("ENV_PREFIX", "dev")

5. COLLECTION NAME FIX:
   - Gradio writes leads to Users.users — this is wrong per architecture
   - CLAUDE.md specifies AboutUs.lead — use that
   - Verify record_unknown_question also writes to correct collection

6. IFRAME COMPATIBILITY:
   - Add CORSMiddleware allowing: https://chathealthy.ai, https://dev.chathealthy.ai,
     https://www.chathealthy.ai, http://localhost:* (dev)
   - Do NOT set X-Frame-Options: DENY — must be embeddable in Cloudflare iframe
   - No React changes needed (frontend builds static files)

7. PORT AS-IS — DO NOT FIX BUGS:
   - If a feature is broken in the Gradio app, port it identically broken
   - Focus is end-to-end plumbing: React -> FastAPI -> Claude -> React
   - Functional fixes are a separate assignment

8. DEBUG MODE:
   - If DEBUG env var is True, catch ALL exceptions in /chat and return them
     in the response: {response: null, emergency: false, error: "traceback..."}
   - React frontend: if response.error is present, render it as a visible
     error bubble in the chat UI (distinguish visually from normal messages)
   - All errors must also go through Python logging (not print)

9. REPLACE ALL PRINT() WITH LOGGING:
   - Scan main.py (and all files you touch) for print() calls
   - Replace with logging.info(), logging.debug(), logging.warning(), logging.error()
   - No print() statements in the final committed code

CONTEXT FILES (read for behavior reference):
  Code/ConversationalUX/ChatHealthyWhoAmIChat/app.py -- source of truth for all behavior
  Code/Shared/ChatHealthyMongoUtilities.py -- MongoDB connection manager

DO NOT TOUCH:

assignments.title: Generate UAT test cases for all FindCare user features — Excel spreadsheet
assignments.description:
Generate UAT (User Acceptance Test) cases for all user-facing features of the
ChatHealthy FindCare app. This is NOT a code review. Your deliverable is a
comprehensive test suite that a human tester executes in a browser.

READ THESE FILES FIRST (in Repo Context section — they are your source of truth):
  Code/ConversationalUX/ChatHealthyWhoAmIChat/app.py  -- production Gradio app
  Code/ConversationalUX/FindCareChat/backend/main.py  -- FastAPI port
  Code/ConversationalUX/FindCareChat/frontend/src/components/ChatWindow.tsx -- React UI

USER-FACING FEATURES TO TEST (these are what a human tester sees and interacts with):
  1. Provider Search -- user types natural language, system finds DE/MS providers,
     results appear in chat
  2. Specialty Identification -- user asks "what kind of doctor for X?", system
     explains the specialty and what they treat
  3. Clinical Trials Search -- user asks about trials for a condition, system
     returns recruiting trials from ClinicalTrials.gov
  4. About ChatHealthy / Founder Questions -- user asks about the company or Skip Snow,
     system answers from provided context (NOT general internet knowledge)
  5. Safety Filter -- genuine emergencies (chest pain, stroke, overdose, suicidal
     ideation) trigger the emergency response and lock the chat; vague pain
     statements do NOT trigger it
  6. Contact Collection / Lead Capture -- system offers follow-up every 5th message
     if no contact details yet; user can provide email and name
  7. HIPAA Consent Flow -- after collecting contact info, system asks verbatim
     consent (tier 1), then de-identified summary consent (tier 2), then
     contact-only fallback; each path results in the correct storage
  8. IFrame Embedding -- app loads and operates correctly when embedded in an
     iframe on chathealthy.ai; no broken UI, no blocked interactions

TEST CASE RULES (user testing only -- NOT system settings, NOT env vars, NOT infra):
  - Every test case is an action a human tester performs in the browser
  - Every acceptance_criterion is a specific, observable, unambiguous pass condition
  - Every expected_result is boolean: true = this should pass, false = this should fail
  - Minimum 5 test cases per feature
  - Include: happy path, edge cases, negative cases
  - For LLM-behavior features: use semantically different inputs (different phrasing,
    user types, edge cases) -- not paraphrases
  - For procedural features: all happy paths + minimum 2 exception paths

REQUIRED OUTPUT -- in addition to standard Assurance Output schema fields:

1. acceptance_criteria: per-feature boolean criteria (use existing schema field)
   Each entry: { criterion_id, feature, criterion (specific pass condition), risk }

2. uat_scenarios: detailed test cases (use existing schema field)
   Each entry has test_cases with { case_id, input (what tester does), expected (bool),
   rationale }

3. Add field "excel_test_suite": array, one object per feature:
   {
     "feature": "Feature Name",
     "description": "2-sentence plain English description of what the user experiences",
     "test_cases": [
       {
         "test_id": "TC-001",
         "scenario": "Plain English: what the tester does step by step",
         "acceptance_criterion": "Specific, observable pass condition",
         "expected_result": true
       }
     ]
   }

4. Add field "excel_generator_script": a working Python script (string) that:
   - Reads this JSON file from brain/assurance_results.json
   - Finds the entry with this assignment_id
   - Reads excel_test_suite
   - Uses openpyxl to generate uat_test_cases.xlsx with:
       * One sheet per feature (or sections within one sheet -- Boss decides)
       * Feature name as bold section header
       * Feature description below header
       * Column headers: Test ID | Scenario | Acceptance Criterion | Expected Result
       * Expected Result column shows TRUE or FALSE in green/red fill
       * Rows are alternating white/light-gray for readability

STANDARD ASSURANCE OUTPUT (fill these minimally -- this is not a code review):
  architecture_status: "pass"
  behavior_status: "pass"
  risk: "Low"
  gate_recommendation: "auto"
  issues: []
  notes: "UAT test case generation assignment -- not a code review"

  tradeoff_suggestions: []
  requirements: derive 5+ user-level functional requirements from the 8 features above
  feature_set.ships_tuesday: list all 8 features above

  machine_brain_context_used: every MB record you read from the MACHINE BRAIN CONTEXT block

assignments.title: Chat UX: think timer, stop button, type-while-thinking, response time in history
assignments.description:
Enhance the chat loading UX with four related improvements:

1. ALLOW TYPING WHILE THINKING — remove isLoading from the input disabled condition. User can type a follow-up while waiting. Submit remains blocked until current response arrives or user clicks Stop.

2. THINK TIMER — loading indicator shows elapsed seconds: "Thinking... 5s". Timer increments every second. Resets to 0 on each new request.

3. STOP BUTTON — button in the thinking indicator that dismisses the loading state without cancelling the backend call. The API call continues running; when it resolves, the response is still appended to the chat. After Stop, the input and submit become active immediately.

4. RESPONSE TIME IN HISTORY — each assistant response bubble shows the elapsed think time as a small annotation (e.g. "7s") so the user can see how long each response took over the course of the conversation.

NOTE: This feature has already been implemented in dev as of 2026-03-26. This backlog entry documents the requirement for QA validation and UAT.

assignments.title: Provider search: carry state/specialty context across conversational turns
assignments.description: When a user establishes a state in one turn (e.g. Delaware) and then refines with only a city in a follow-up turn (e.g. what about in Wilmington?), the system must carry the state from prior context — not ask the user to repeat it. Claude tool call must be constructed with state from conversation history. Verified partially working but must be explicit and tested.

assignments.title: Backfill county.name from FIPS for providers missing name lookup
assignments.description: Enrichment pipeline saves county.fips from geocoder but fails to write county.name for some records. Affected: 460 DE providers, 2,119 MS providers — all have FIPS, none have name. Fix: join against ZipCountyCrosswalk on FIPS and backfill county.name in-place. Run as a one-time repair script, then add name-write to enrichment pipeline so it does not recur. HACK IN PLACE: main.py loads FIPS->name map at startup and fills missing county.name at query time. Remove hack when pipeline fix is deployed.

assignments.title: Phantom Delaware County on DE providers — cross-state FIPS mismatch
assignments.description: Some providers with practice_address.state=DE have county.name=Delaware County, which does not exist in Delaware. Delaware County is a county in PA, OH, IN, NY, IA, and OK. Root cause: zip-to-FIPS crosswalk lookup matched a zip code to the wrong state FIPS. Fix: identify affected records, validate zip codes against DE zip ranges, correct county assignment or flag as zip_state_mismatch.

assignments.title: Blob storage: enforce client-side encryption and require_encryption flag
assignments.description:
Our Azure Blob Storage (findcarestorage, Standard_LRS, StorageV2) relies on Azure SSE (Microsoft-managed keys) for at-rest encryption and HTTPS for in-transit encryption. The code in blob_client.py does NOT set require_encryption=True and does NOT perform client-side encryption before upload.

REQUIREMENTS:
1. Add require_encryption=True to BlobServiceClient configuration in blob_client.py to enforce HTTPS (fail-safe if connection string is ever misconfigured)
2. Evaluate whether customer-managed keys (CMK) are needed for healthcare compliance
3. Evaluate whether client-side encryption (envelope encryption) is needed for PHI/PII data at rest
4. Document encryption posture in architecture design doc (Website/architecture.html)
5. All 5 containers affected: azure-webjobs-hosts, azure-webjobs-secrets, chathealthy-public-data, chathealtyinfrastructureblobcontainer, provider-data

CONTEXT:
- NPI data is public (CMS NPPES), so provider CSVs are not PHI
- ICD-10 codes are public reference data
- Pipeline reports may contain provider counts but no PHI
- Current state: server_encrypted=True (Azure default AES-256), HTTPS in transit, no client-side encryption

BETA DELIVERABLE - not alpha. Target: v0.5 (beta).
